parameters.content:
## 1 · Intake and normalise

The bot receives *anything*: a forwarded reel, a link, a screenshot, or typed text.

**Config** is the only node you edit to retune this workflow - paths, model, base URL, limits.

**Normalise Input** collapses every possible Telegram message into one flat shape
(`input_type`, `work_dir`, `telegram_file_id`, `source_url`, ...). Nothing after this node
ever reads `$json.message` again - it reads `$('Normalise Input')`.

`work_dir` contains a random run id, so two reels arriving at the same second
cannot overwrite each other.

## 2 · Acquire the media

**Uploaded video** -> Telegram `file:get` (binary) -> written to disk. Bot API caps
downloads at 20 MB, which `Normalise Input` already checks for.

**Link** -> `yt-dlp`. Handles Instagram reels/posts/TV, YouTube Shorts, TikTok and more.
It is allowed to fail: `Download OK?` inspects the exit code instead of the node throwing,
so a private or deleted post produces a Telegram reply, not a dead execution.

Both paths end with `video.mp4` inside `work_dir`, then meet at **Media Ready**.

parameters.command:
=set -e
D='{{ $('Normalise Input').item.json.work_dir }}'
cd "$D"
yt-dlp --no-playlist --no-warnings --no-progress --no-part \
  --max-filesize {{ $('Config').item.json.max_download_mb }}M \
  -S "res:720,ext:mp4:m4a" --merge-output-format mp4 \
  {{ $('Config').item.json.ytdlp_extra }} \
  -o 'src.%(ext)s' -- '{{ $('Normalise Input').item.json.source_url }}' 2>&1 | tail -n 8
f=$(ls -1 src.* 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
if [ -z "$f" ]; then echo "yt-dlp produced no file (private, removed, rate-limited, or over the size cap)"; exit 1; fi
mv -- "$f" video.mp4
echo "downloaded $(du -h video.mp4 | cut -f1)"

parameters.content:
## 3 · Understand the video

`ffmpeg` pulls a 16 kHz mono wav; `whisper.cpp` transcribes it locally (free, no API).

Both nodes are allowed to fail softly. A reel with **no speech** yields an empty
transcript and the run continues on frames alone - that is the common case, not an error.

`Extract Frames` samples 1 frame every `frame_every_seconds`, caps at `max_frames`,
scales to 512 px, and base64-encodes them to stdout - one frame per line. That keeps the
images entirely inside the item stream; no extra binary plumbing.

parameters.command:
=D='{{ $('Normalise Input').item.json.work_dir }}'
cd "$D" || exit 1
if [ ! -f video.mp4 ]; then echo "video.mp4 missing"; exit 1; fi
ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i video.mp4 -vn -ac 1 -ar 16000 audio.wav 2>&1 | tail -n 3
if [ -f audio.wav ]; then echo "audio ok"; else echo "no audio stream in this video"; fi
exit 0

=D='{{ $('Normalise Input').item.json.work_dir }}'
W='{{ $('Config').item.json.whisper_bin }}'
M='{{ $('Config').item.json.whisper_model }}'
if [ -f "$D/audio.wav" ] && [ -x "$W" ]; then
  "$W" -m "$M" -f "$D/audio.wav" -nt -otxt -of "$D/transcript" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
if [ -f "$D/transcript.txt" ]; then cat "$D/transcript.txt"; fi
exit 0

=D='{{ $('Normalise Input').item.json.work_dir }}'
cd "$D" || exit 1
ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i video.mp4 \
  -vf "fps=1/{{ $('Config').item.json.frame_every_seconds }},scale=512:-2" \
  -frames:v {{ $('Config').item.json.max_frames }} -q:v 4 'frame_%02d.jpg' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
for f in frame_*.jpg; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  base64 -w 0 "$f"
  echo ""
done
exit 0

parameters.content:
## 4 · Screenshots and plain text

A **photo** has no audio and no motion, so it skips ffmpeg/whisper entirely: download,
save as `frame_01.jpg`, base64 it, empty transcript. The vision model does the rest.

**Plain text** skips media altogether - the typed text becomes the "transcript" and gets
classified and filed just like a reel. Typing "try htmx on the Fable admin" files a to-do.

All three paths converge on the same shape: `{ transcript, frames_b64 }`.

parameters.command:
=D='{{ $('Normalise Input').item.json.work_dir }}'
if [ -f "$D/frame_01.jpg" ]; then base64 -w 0 "$D/frame_01.jpg"; echo ""; fi
exit 0

parameters.content:
## 5 · Classify with a free LLM (the routing brain)

**Default: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash on the free tier** - native vision, free, and it speaks
the OpenAI chat/completions dialect, so the request body is provider-neutral.

**To swap provider, change TWO things in the Config node and ONE credential:**
| provider | llm_base_url | llm_model |
|---|---|---|
| Gemini (default) | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai` | `gemini-2.5-flash` |
| Groq | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | `meta-llama/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct` |
| OpenRouter | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free` |
| Ollama (same VPS) | `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` | `llama3.2-vision` |

The credential is a generic **Header Auth**: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Same node works
for all four. `Classify` never throws: `neverError` + `fullResponse` hand the status code to
`Parse Classification`, which strips fences, retries the widest `{...}` span, coerces every
field, and forces low-confidence results to the to-do path flagged `#needs-review`.

nodes.name: Note: 5 · Classify with a free LLM (the routing brain)

parameters.content:
## 6 · Route to one of four destinations

The four branch nodes do one thing each: pick the target note and tag the entry kind.
All the formatting and all the git work is shared below, so there is one copy of it.

- **skill** -> `SKILLS-INBOX.md` - install command + a verification step.
  n8n *cannot* install a Claude Code skill on your laptop. It writes a paste-ready command.
- **todo** -> `TODO.md` - checkbox list you read each morning. Low-confidence lands here.
- **design** -> `DESIGN.md` - visual takeaways.
- **reference** -> `REFERENCE.md` - keep, nothing to do.
- **discard** -> no file written, just a Telegram note so you know it was seen.

nodes.name: Note: 6 · Route to one of four destinations

parameters.content:
## 7 · Get it into the Obsidian vault (git)

The vault lives on the **laptop**; n8n runs on the **VPS**. A VPS cannot write to
`C:\OBSIDIAN VAULT`. So: the vault is a private git repo, the VPS holds a clone at
`vault_repo`, n8n appends + commits + pushes, and the **Obsidian Git plugin** on the
laptop pulls every few minutes.

Why git and not OneDrive/local n8n: it is the only option that survives the laptop being
off, needs no tunnel or open port, and gives a full history plus real conflict handling.
Cost: one extra `git pull` step, and merge conflicts if you edit the same note at the
same second (`--autostash` + append-only writes make that very unlikely).

**Security:** the model's output goes into a FILE and is appended with `cat`. It is never
interpolated into a shell command. The only interpolated value is `note_file`, a fixed
string from the four branch nodes.

nodes.name: Note: 7 · Get it into the Obsidian vault (git)

parameters.command:
=set -e
D='{{ $('Normalise Input').item.json.work_dir }}'
R='{{ $('Config').item.json.vault_repo }}'
B='{{ $('Config').item.json.git_branch }}'
F='{{ $('Render Entry').item.json.note_file }}'
cd "$R"
git config --local user.name '{{ $('Config').item.json.git_user }}'
git config --local user.email '{{ $('Config').item.json.git_email }}'
git fetch -q origin "$B"
git checkout -q "$B"
git pull -q --rebase --autostash origin "$B"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$F")"
if [ ! -f "$F" ]; then printf '# %s\n' "$(basename "$F" .md)" > "$F"; fi
cat "$D/entry.md" >> "$F"
git add -- "$F"
if git diff --cached --quiet; then echo "nothing changed"; exit 0; fi
git commit -q -m "reel-bot: {{ $('Normalise Input').item.json.run_id }}"
git push -q origin "$B"
echo "committed to $F"

parameters.content:
## 8 · Reply, then always clean up

Every path ends in a Telegram message - success, discard, or failure. Silence is a bug.

**Build Failure Message** has four inputs (bad input, download failed, classifier failed,
vault write failed) and works out which one fired from the fields on the item, so there is
one failure node instead of four.

**Cleanup** has three inputs and runs on every path, including failures, so `/tmp/reels`
never fills up. The `case` guard means an empty expression can never turn this into
`rm -rf /`.

nodes.name: Note: 8 · Reply, then always clean up
